summary: Discovery call with Proxima Bank exploring Redwood Dedicated reserved GPU capacity. Key themes: isolation/data residency, burst strategy for peak trading hours, predictable throughput for 99th percentile latency SLOs, PKI/KMS for keys, SOC2 and audit logs. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated w/ private VPC but wants to validate performance and cost vs hosted and in-house. Agreed next steps: pricing, benchmarks, and PoC kickoff.
topics: Security: KMS, SOC2, RBAC, audit logs
transcript:
Header: 2026-08-18 14:30 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Carlos (CTO), Evelyn (Head of ML), Samir (Infra), Lena (Security)

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can folks introduce quickly?
[00:08] Carlos: Carlos here, CTO, super quick we want to understand options — hosted vs dedicated vs private — mostly leaning dedicated for isolation.
[00:15] Jamie: Great, that's our sweet spot. Ravi and Maya from our SE team will cover sizing and burst patterns.
[00:22] Ravi: Hey all. Quick agenda: current infra, workloads and QPS, latency SLOs, security needs, and PoC next steps.
[00:30] Evelyn: For context our models are a mix — a few open LLMs fine-tuned for summarization and AML alerts. Typical seq lengths 512-1k, occasional 2k. We expect spikes during market open, maybe 3x baseline for 10-20 minutes.
[00:45] Samir: Right now everything's on-prem in our private cloud but we do have sensitive PII so isolation and encryption at rest is a must.
[00:52] Maya: Understood — Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and a private VPC option. We can provision dedicated nodes only for Proxima so no noisy neighbors.
[01:05] Lena: Can you talk about KMS/HSM? We need key separation and customer-managed keys.
[01:12] Ravi: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault), HSM can be supported for private deployments. We'll provide audit logs and key usage metadata.
[01:20] Carlos: How do you handle burst capacity? If we reserve say 8 GPUs for baseline how do we handle spikes?
[01:30] Jamie: We have two levers — burst licenses and autoscaling policies. For Dedicated you can reserve steady capacity and allow bursts into a shared pool or pay-per-burst above the commit.
[01:40] Samir: Is the burst pool noisy-neighbor protected? We can't have other tenants impact our latency.
[01:48] Ravi: Good point — bursts into our shared pool have priority tiers; you can choose guaranteed burst (reserved spare capacity) vs best-effort. For strict isolation we recommend a mix: baseline dedicated + guaranteed burst or a secondary reserved pool.
[02:05] Evelyn: Latency is critical. 99th percentile under 200ms for short prompts, and sub-second for longer streaming responses. Is that realistic?
[02:18] Maya: With the right GPU class and batching profile yes; sequence length and batch sizes drive tail latency. We'll recommend kernel/quantization options. Note: continuum batch and KV cache improve throughput but can add small tail latency — we can tune.
[02:35] Carlos: You mentioned KV cache — is that persistent across restarts?
[02:40] Ravi: KV cache persists during runtime; in some infra events it flushes. Also, sorry my notes say KV "cash" in my earlier doc — transcription quirk there.
[02:50] Lena: What compliance artifacts do you provide? SOC2, ISO, pen-test?
[02:55] Jamie: SOC2 Type II, ISO summaries are available; we also have pen test reports on request and can provide network diagrams and RBAC role mappings. We'll share the security packet after this call.
[03:05] Samir: How about data residency — can Dedicated be hosted in our GCP region in eu-west-1?
[03:12] Ravi: Yes, Dedicated can be region pin; for Private deployments we can run in your VPC or on-prem depending on the contract. There is an added ops overhead for on-prem packaging.
[03:25] Evelyn: For model updates — can we pin model versions and roll back? We need stable regression guardrails.
[03:32] Maya: Absolutely — Dedicated supports model version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallbacks to smaller variants if larger models exceed SLOs.
[03:45] Carlos: Pricing — do you price by token / reserved GPU hours / or both?
[03:52] Jamie: For Hosted it's usage-based; for Dedicated we do a committed capacity model (monthly/annual) plus a unit price for burst or overage. We'll send the SKU/pricing sheet.
[04:05] Carlos: For the PoC we want to validate both throughput and quality. We will run our validation prompts including AML cases and check hallucination rates.
[04:15] Ravi: Great, we'll need a representative prompt set and sample traffic patterns. We'll run benchmarks on a similar instance class, share the perf sheet, and run a two-week PoC with telemetry.
[04:28] Evelyn: Any known limitations with quantized models for our use-case? We need token-level fidelity for legal language.
[04:36] Maya: Quantization can impact generation fidelity slightly for rare tokens; we typically recommend int8 for most tasks but keep int16 for exacting legal text. We'll show quality regressions vs cost tradeoffs in the benchmark.
[04:50] Samir: Ops integration — do you offer Prometheus metrics, tracing hooks, and token-level billing exports?
[04:57] Ravi: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route token cost, latency breakdown, traces, and we can export to your observability stack. There may be minor naming mismatches in the telemetry that we can map.
[05:10] Lena: SSO & RBAC — SAML/Okta support?
[05:14] Jamie: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, granular RBAC — yes. We also support audit log streaming to your SIEM.
[05:22] Carlos: What's the timeline to get a PoC environment? We need to test before end of quarter.
[05:28] Jamie: If we get access to a few test endpoints and the prompt set this week we can spin up a dedicated pool and run initial perf tests in 7-10 days.
[05:36] Maria: (silence)
[05:40] Evelyn: Are there any vendors you recommend for hybrid on-prem packaging?
[05:44] Ravi: We have partner references; depending on your data center we can recommend a partner for appliance-style deployment.
[05:50] Carlos: Any gotchas in network egress costs? If model weights are large and we pull them often will that be an ongoing cost?
[05:58] Maya: We typically cache weights on node local storage; weight pull happens on deployment or scale-up events. For Dedicated steady-state you shouldn't see repeated weight pulls unless you change models frequently.
[06:12] Samir: Can we pre-warm models before market open to avoid cold-start latency?
[06:16] Ravi: Yes, pre-warming is supported; we can keep warmers or maintain idle KV cache. There's a cost tradeoff but it's common for trading windows.
[06:28] Carlos: Ok let's map numbers. Our baseline expected QPS is 120 requests/min with p50 latency ~120ms, spikes up to 360 req/min for 15 minutes.
[06:40] Ravi: For 512-1k seqs that's moderate; my back-of-envelope says 8 A100-class GPUs with optimized batching and caching could cover base, but spikes might need guaranteed burst of 4 GPUs. We'll validate in benchmarks.
[06:58] Evelyn: We also want to run an eval for hallucination and a side-by-side with our current in-house infra to compare.
[07:05] Jamie: Totally, we'll include comparison steps.
[07:12] (crosstalk) Alex: procurement question — contract minimums?
[07:16] Jamie: Typically monthly minimums for Dedicated and annual discounts for committed. We'll put ranges in the pricing doc.
[07:25] Lena: Another security Q: Are audit logs immutable and retained for 12 months?
[07:30] Ravi: We can retain logs per contract; immutable write-once logs can be set up to satisfy your retention. We'll share specifics.
[07:40] Carlos: For the PoC success criteria: 99p latency below 300ms for our critical route, throughput to handle peak spike, and no regression in hallucination rate vs baseline.
[07:52] Jamie: We'll codify that in the runbook.
[08:00] Evelyn: Any enablement for our ML team to tune prompts or batcher configs?
[08:06] Maya: We'll provide recommended batching profiles and tuning sessions with our SEs. Also include guidance on prefix caching and prompt templating.
[08:18] Carlos: Ok last— how do you handle model refreshes for security patches?
[08:22] Ravi: We handle model updates as flagged maintenance windows by default; for Dedicated we can schedule updates with you, and maintain pinned versions until you approve.
[08:35] Jamie: Cool, to recap action items and next steps...
[08:38] Jamie: We'll share pricing, security packet (SOC2, ISO, pen-tests), and benchmark template. SEs will prep PoC runbook and request prompt set + QPS curves.
[08:50] Carlos: Sounds good. We'll aim to provide prompt set and traffic profile by 2026-08-22.
[08:55] Jamie: Perfect; let's pencil PoC kickoff for 2026-08-25.
[09:00] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription includes a few mis-heard terms (KV "cash"), occasional speaker label flips (Maria vs Maya), and run-on sentences typical for transcripts. The detailed benchmark sheet link and pricing doc to be attached separately.
